title: OtaconsKeep Continuity Model
honesty: The Continuity Model (CM-01…CM-25) is the design theory for behavioral continuity. Runtime modules implement a subset today (emotional continuity + Formula 5). Worked traces labeled MOCK are synthetic. This page does not claim human consciousness — it claims measurable, bounded state dynamics.
manual_note: The OtaconsKeep continuity model is derived from a practical blend of trait psychology, appraisal-based emotion logic, memory relevance scoring, relationship reinforcement, and state regulation principles. It does not claim to reproduce human consciousness. Instead, it uses mathematically simple but psychologically grounded mechanisms to simulate continuity, emotional carryover, social weighting, and context-sensitive behavior over time. The original equations define the behavioral engine. Stability-layer equations (caps, identity anchor, output evaluation) bound per-cycle change, preserve identity, limit memory dominance, and evaluate output quality.
diluted_version: It feels different depending on what happened
Then it decides what to say or do

rationale.title: Why this emulates continuity (not consciousness)
body: Human-like persistence is approximated by carrying a state vector, relationship graph, and memory scores across turns — the opposite of stateless autocomplete.
Multiplication models interaction (pain × trauma relevance); summation models accumulation (many events in one cycle).
Decay and baselines model regulation / homeostasis so affect does not spiral forever.
Bounded noise prevents robotic sameness without becoming chaos.
Identity anchor (β_i ≥ β_min) keeps character from dissolving under adaptation.

Markov stage labels and OR goal programs add probabilistic and decision-theoretic structure on top of the continuous engine — useful for analysis, planning, and V&V — without replacing the continuous math.

core_logic_justification.multiplication: Used when one factor should amplify or dampen another (event hurt × trauma; praise × trust; trait × trigger).
core_logic_justification.summation: Used when multiple inputs all contribute (many events on mood; many social signals; competing memories).
core_logic_justification.decay: Pulls values toward baseline so the system recovers and stays long-run stable.
core_logic_justification.bounded_noise: Small η prevents identical replies while remaining coherent.

chapters.title: Trait Weight Model
katex: W_t = B_D \cdot S_t \cdot C_t \cdot P_t \cdot K_t \cdot (1+\varepsilon_t)
chapters.meaning: Converts a written dossier trait into a usable numeric weight.
chapters.why_this_logic: Multiplicative model: traits do not stack flatly — they amplify or weaken each other by category, certainty, personality, and context. Example: PTSD weighs more than coffee dependence; inferred traits weigh less than canonical; same trait matters differently across personalities.
chapters.why_these_variables: B_D = category seriousness; S_t = not all trauma/habits equal; C_t = known vs guessed; P_t = personality changes expression; K_t = context; ε_t = avoid robotic sameness.
chapters.simple_explanation: How strong is this trait for this agent?

chapters.title: Active Trait Influence Model
chapters.meaning: Decides whether a trait matters right now.
chapters.why_this_logic: A strong trait should not always dominate. It becomes active when something triggers it, the right person is involved, and memory makes it relevant.
chapters.why_these_variables: G = triggers activate latent traits; R = traits hit differently by who is involved; M = recent/emotional memories amplify relevance.
chapters.simple_explanation: Does this trait matter in this moment?

chapters.title: Event Impact on State
chapters.meaning: Calculates how events change an internal state variable (mood, stress, confidence, …).

variables.def: total change in state X at time t
set of events active at time t
base effect of event e on state X

chapters.why_this_logic: Summation over events (many things can affect someone at once). Multiplication inside each event (raw effect filtered by personality, relationships, history).
chapters.why_these_variables: E = event strength; Q = personalities react differently; L = who caused it matters; H = past pain amplifies impact.
chapters.simple_explanation: How much did what just happened affect me?

chapters.title: State Update Model
chapters.meaning: Updates an internal state over time with event drive, noise, decay-to-baseline, and bounds.
chapters.why_this_logic: Dynamic system: events move state; noise prevents robotic sameness; decay pulls toward baseline; clamp prevents runaway.
chapters.why_these_variables: η = humans are not perfectly deterministic; λ = emotions settle; X* = natural baseline.
chapters.simple_explanation: How do I feel now after everything that happened?

chapters.title: Relationship Update Model
chapters.meaning: Updates a relationship dimension toward target j (trust, admiration, resentment, …).
chapters.why_this_logic: Relationships change gradually through repeated events with inertia — avoid unrealistic instant swings.
chapters.why_these_variables: ΔY = events strengthen/weaken bonds; μ = sticky relationships; Y* = natural trust bias.
chapters.simple_explanation: Do I trust or resent this person more now?

chapters.title: Social Influence Model
chapters.meaning: Measures how social posts, comments, messages, or public signals affect an agent.
chapters.why_this_logic: Not all social signals matter equally — tone, public/private, source, and sensitivity interact.
chapters.why_these_variables: V = tone; U = public hits harder; L = some people matter more; Z = absorption differs by agent.
chapters.simple_explanation: How much did that post or message affect me?

chapters.title: Emotional Residue Model
chapters.meaning: Models leftover emotional carryover from earlier events.
chapters.why_this_logic: People do not reset after each event — some feeling remains and carries forward.
chapters.why_these_variables: ρ = traces persist; ω = events leave different residue amounts.
chapters.simple_explanation: Am I still carrying the feeling from earlier?

chapters.title: Emotion Selection Model
chapters.meaning: Chooses the best-fitting emotion label from the current state vector.

variables.def: weight of state i for emotion k

chapters.why_this_logic: Emotions are combinations of mood/stress/confidence/belonging/control — project state into emotion-space and pick the strongest match.
chapters.why_these_variables: α = each emotion depends on different state combinations; X = internal state drives displayed feeling.
chapters.simple_explanation: What emotion fits best right now?

chapters.title: Memory Retrieval Score
chapters.meaning: Scores how relevant a memory or context item is for the current response.
chapters.why_this_logic: Weighted linear score: simple, tunable, interpretable, debuggable. Favors relevant/recent/emotional memories; suppresses stale repetition.
chapters.why_these_variables: T/P/E/R/N cover topic, person, emotion, recency, novelty.
chapters.simple_explanation: What should I remember for this moment?

chapters.title: Agent–Device Relevance Model
chapters.meaning: Decides whether an agent should care about a device, service, VM, mount, or hardware component.

variables.def: relevance of device d to agent a

chapters.why_this_logic: Avoid hardcoded awareness for every future device — inherit awareness from responsibility tags × device tags × criticality.
chapters.why_these_variables: Ω = role matching; P_d = critical systems matter more.
chapters.simple_explanation: Is this thing part of my job?

chapters.title: Full System Output Function
chapters.meaning: Master output function combining continuity layers into final response/behavior.
chapters.why_this_logic: Compositional system: output must not come from one prompt alone — identity, feeling, relationships, memory, domain, history, and task all contribute.
chapters.why_these_variables: Each term is a continuity layer that would otherwise be lost in stateless autocomplete.
chapters.simple_explanation: Given who I am, what I remember, how I feel, and what’s happening — what should I say or do?

summary_equation.meaning: Plain-language summary of the whole model.
summary_equation.simple: Why does the system feel alive? Because it does not reset — it carries forward who it is, what happened, and how that changed it.

chapters.title: Input Normalization Model
chapters.meaning: Maps raw inputs into a unit interval so heterogeneous signals share a common scale.
chapters.why_this_logic: Without normalization, loud channels dominate soft ones for no psychological reason.
chapters.why_these_variables: Min/max define the operating range for each channel.
chapters.simple_explanation: Put every signal on the same yardstick.

chapters.title: Event Delta Cap Model
chapters.meaning: Hard-limits per-event state change so a single message cannot nuke the agent.
chapters.why_this_logic: Stability layer: one outlier event should not erase years of relationship mass.
chapters.why_these_variables: δ_e is a design guardrail, not a personality trait.
chapters.simple_explanation: How hard can one event hit?

chapters.title: Trait Contribution Cap Model
chapters.meaning: Bounds total active trait influence so trait stacks cannot overwhelm identity.
chapters.why_this_logic: Many active traits can otherwise drown the voice — cap preserves character.
chapters.why_these_variables: Sum accumulates; clip enforces ceiling.
chapters.simple_explanation: How much trait pressure is allowed this cycle?

chapters.title: Identity Anchor Model
chapters.meaning: Blends stable identity output with adaptive continuity output; identity never drops below a floor.
chapters.why_this_logic: Without an identity floor, long runs drift into whoever the last event rewarded.
chapters.why_these_variables: β_min is the non-negotiable self.
chapters.simple_explanation: Stay yourself while still adapting.

chapters.title: Output Evaluation Model
chapters.meaning: Scores output quality for learning / adaptation feedback.
chapters.why_this_logic: You cannot adapt what you cannot score. Coherence × state fit × relationship fit.
chapters.why_these_variables: Weights express which failure mode matters more in a given product surface.
chapters.simple_explanation: Was that reply any good?

chapters.title: Social Cycle Cap Model
chapters.meaning: Caps aggregate social impact per cycle so pile-ons cannot force runaway affect.
chapters.why_this_logic: Public channels can spam; the agent must remain regulable.
chapters.why_these_variables: Clip after sum — many weak signals still accumulate, then hit a ceiling.
chapters.simple_explanation: How much social weather am I allowed to absorb right now?

chapters.title: Goal Selection Model
chapters.meaning: Selects the active goal the agent should pursue at time t.
chapters.why_this_logic: Move from reactive → purpose-driven: score goals, pick highest utility.
chapters.why_these_variables: S = current needs; C = personality priorities; D = domain (ARR/HA/…); H = history.
chapters.simple_explanation: What should I try to do right now?

chapters.title: Goal Utility Function
chapters.meaning: Calculates how valuable a goal is.
chapters.why_this_logic: Goals should reflect urgency, importance, and personality — not randomness.
chapters.why_these_variables: Weights make tradeoffs explicit and tunable.
chapters.simple_explanation: How important is this goal?

chapters.title: Conflict Resolution Model
chapters.meaning: Resolves competing influences into a single dominant driver.
chapters.why_this_logic: Without this, the system blends everything and becomes mush. Force a decision, not an average.
chapters.why_these_variables: Weights encode which continuity layer wins under conflict.
chapters.simple_explanation: What matters most right now?

chapters.title: Learning / Adaptation Model
chapters.meaning: Adjusts system parameters based on output quality.
chapters.why_this_logic: Improve over time: reduce bad outputs, reinforce good behavior — without rewriting identity.
chapters.why_these_variables: α small → stable; α large → brittle. Bound updates.
chapters.simple_explanation: Did I do well, and should I adjust?

chapters.title: Memory Tier Weighting Model
chapters.meaning: Scales memory importance by tier so identity memories outrank routine noise.
chapters.why_this_logic: Not all memories should compete equally.
chapters.why_these_variables: Tier weights encode autobiographical priority.
chapters.simple_explanation: Which memories matter more?

chapters.title: Uncertainty Propagation Model
chapters.meaning: Reduces influence of low-confidence traits.
chapters.why_this_logic: Guessed traits should whisper; canonical traits may speak. Uncertainty damps.
chapters.why_these_variables: Multiplication by C is the simplest honest uncertainty gate.
chapters.simple_explanation: How sure am I that this trait should drive me?

chapters.title: Markov Affect Transition Model
chapters.meaning: Treats discrete emotional stage labels as a Markov chain whose transition matrix depends on the event class and personality.
chapters.why_this_logic: Continuous state E(t) is primary; stage labels are a readout. Markov T explains stage-to-stage jumps (see STM-002) without inventing consciousness — only transition structure.
chapters.why_these_variables: Event-conditioned rows encode appraisal; personality stretches holding times (inertia).
chapters.simple_explanation: Given how I feel labeled now, where can I go next?

chapters.title: Operations-Research Goal Program (OR)
chapters.meaning: Casts goal selection as a constrained utility program over feasible actions in the current domain (ARR, HA, Codec, install).
chapters.why_this_logic: OR framing makes tradeoffs explicit: urgency vs risk vs character alignment under resource caps — same math used in scheduling and multi-objective programming.
chapters.why_these_variables: Constraints stop wishful goals (e.g. Video Studio when Docker/GPU not READY).
chapters.simple_explanation: What’s the best feasible thing I can attempt with what I have?

markov_or_notes.title: Probabilistic & operations-research layer
markov_or_notes.body: CM-24 treats stage labels as a Markov chain for analysis and STM diagrams. CM-25 casts goal choice as a constrained utility / goal program. Neither invents PASS results; both are design models for V&V scenarios and planning analysis.
